checked: HRL, IHL, jurisdiction, IAC, NIAC, organization, and intensity are explained before the classification examples. ICCPR is first signposted as the later rules and then fully named before its treaty conditions are needed.
Derogation and non-derogable rights have local meanings. Contract is defined before the debt-protection list; servitude, retroactive punishment, and conscience are glossed at first teaching use.

Hors de combat, means/methods, indiscriminate weapons, unnecessary suffering, distinction, military objective, proportionality, incidental harm, precautions, and grave breaches are explained before worked application. No prerequisite lesson is needed.

HRL and IHL have purposes, scopes, and bound parties, with classification tests and examples. Complementarity is explained through continuing HRL duties, battlefield targeting, and joint custody protection.

Article 4 teaching explains how temporary suspension works, lists protected rights, and separates suspension from ordinary limits. Weapons and attack concepts explain the decision each rule requires. Peacetime teaching and legislation have named compliance actions; peaceful agreement has a concrete process.
IAC does not require a declaration, occupation can apply without resistance, and NIAC requires both intensity and organization. Ordinary unrest is not automatically armed conflict.

Civilian protection has a direct-participation exception; out-of-fight protection requires no hostile act or escape attempt. Military objectives require both stated conditions. Proportionality is distinct from direct civilian targeting; feasible precautions and cancellation remain required despite warnings.

Emergency teaching includes proclamation, national-life threat, strict necessity, duration, other international duties, discrimination grounds, immediate and ending notices, and non-derogable rights. It also distinguishes ordinary limits on religious practice from suspension of belief protection.

All flagged ICCPR and NIAC uses are real acronyms, as are HRL, IHL, IAC, and UN. Defined legal terms are bold at their explanatory introductions. There is no all-capitals emphasis or excessive italics.
